podcast.body: This was a "funky chatty" top 10 hit for Joe Tex in 1967. Years after a violent incident involving James Brown, Tex claimed in interviews that Brown had tried to sabotage the chart rise of this song. James Brown later co-opted the main lyric of this song for his 1969 hit "Mother Popcorn." "In interviews, Tex questioned Brown's soul brother number one nickname, and claimed that Brown had tried to sabotage the chart rise of his funky chatty 1967 top 10 hit, Skinny Legs and All."
